title: Father, forgive them (Luke 23:34)
hook: for they know not what they do

segments.voice: Yesterday, green wood: on the road, he turned and answered the women's tears. Your line was weep for yourselves.

The place is called Calvary, the skull. Two criminals are led out with him, one on his right and one on his left. Luke tells it almost without detail: they crucified him there. No nails described, no long account of pain. Soon the soldiers will be casting lots for his clothes. And into that ordinary cruelty, the first thing Luke has Jesus say from the cross is not a cry of pain and not a curse. It's a prayer, and it begins with today's word.
screen: `A PLACE CALLED CALVARY.` → `TWO CRIMINALS, ONE EACH SIDE.` → `THE FIRST WORD FROM THE CROSS.`

segments.voice: In the Douay-Rheims: "And Jesus said: Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do." Start with Father. Jesus has called God Father all through Luke: at twelve in the temple, I must be about my Father's business; in the garden, Father, if thou wilt. Nailed to wood, he still prays the same way. The relationship holds, even here. Then, forgive them. Who is them? Luke doesn't say. The soldiers, surely, who are doing the nailing. Some readers widen it to everyone who brought him here. Then the reason: they know not what they do. Not that it's fine, or that it doesn't matter. Only that they don't fully see what they're doing. Catholic devotion counts this as the first of the Seven Last Words, sayings of Jesus from the cross gathered from all four Gospels, and some parishes keep a Good Friday devotion that preaches on them one by one. And Luke shows the prayer didn't end at the cross. In his second book, Acts, the deacon Stephen, dying under stones, prays nearly the same prayer for the people throwing them. It's the hardest forgiveness there is, given while the hurt is still happening.
screen: `FATHER, EVEN HERE.` · `FORGIVE THEM: WHO IS THEM?` · `THE FIRST OF SEVEN LAST WORDS.` · `STEPHEN PRAYS IT TOO.` · then, large: `FOR THEY KNOW NOT WHAT THEY DO.`

segments.voice: Think of someone who hurt you without understanding it, a parent who said the wrong thing, a friend who never noticed what they missed, a careless stranger, and hold them in mind with the words they know not. It doesn't excuse what happened, and it doesn't mean you have to go back. If you pray, use the prayer from the cross for them; if not, just loosen your grip a little.
Father. The first word of the first saying from the cross in Luke: Father, forgive them. In Greek, pater. Today's word.
Your line: they know not. Not an excuse; only the reason he gave. Day four hundred eighty-five.

howItsDone: Catholics hear Luke 23:34 in the Passion on Palm Sunday in the year of Luke, and some parishes keep a Good Friday devotion on the Seven Last Words, of which this is counted the first.

chat.says: How could Jesus forgive the people crucifying him while they were still doing it?
options: He prayed, Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do, even as it happened.
He forgave only the soldiers who later came and asked him for forgiveness.
He said it after he rose, once the pain was over and he could look back.
chat.meaning: Luke's first word from the cross is a prayer: Father, forgive them. Not that it's fine, only that they don't fully see what they do.

notes: The word 'Father' is the outline's title head (the outline has no word). Kept exactly.
Textual note: Luke 23:34a is absent from P75, Codex Vaticanus and others; present in Sinaiticus (original hand) and many witnesses. Stated generally; confirm wording suits the path.
'I must be about my Father's business' (Luke 2:49) and 'Father, if thou wilt' (22:42) are paraphrased in the voice without quotation marks; confirm.
Seven Last Words and the Tre Ore Good Friday devotion: described as kept by many parishes. Confirm.
'The first thing Luke has Jesus say from the cross': confirm (23:28–31 is on the road, before crucifixion).
